Analyze a rectangular beam cross-section under sagging bending using small-deformation linear-elastic assumptions.
The beam width is b = 50 mm and the height is h = 120 mm.
The applied bending moment at the section is M = 4,000,000 N·mm, sagging and taken as positive.
Use N–mm–MPa units throughout.
Measure y from the neutral axis, which coincides with the horizontal centroidal axis, with y positive upward.
Use the standard flexure formula σ = M·y / I with second moment of area I = b·h³/12.
With the sagging moment, bending stress is compressive (negative) above the neutral axis and tensile (positive) below it.
Compute I = 50·120³/12 = 7,200,000 mm⁴.
Compute the bending stress at y = 0 mm (neutral axis), which must equal 0 MPa.
Compute the bending stress at the top fiber y = +60 mm, which must be compressive: σ = 4,000,000·(+60)/7,200,000 = −33.33 MPa.
Compute the bending stress at the bottom fiber y = −60 mm, which must be tensile: σ = 4,000,000·(−60)/7,200,000 = +33.33 MPa.
Present the governing relation σ = M·y / I, the section property I = b·h³/12, and the three stress values with signs consistent with the stated convention.
Assume the material is homogeneous, isotropic, and linear-elastic, plane sections remain plane, and the bending is pure (no shear or axial force at the section).
